articles.headline: Big Week 3 losses: Seahawks, Pats, Texans, Chargers, Panthers
articles.description: The Pats got blown out. The Seahawks lost to a QB2. The Panthers couldn't overcome injuries. The Chargers and Texans fell to 0-3. What now for five of last season's playoff teams?
articles.headlineJa: 第3週の大きな敗戦：シーホークス、ペイトリオッツ、テキサンズ、チャージャーズ、パンサーズ
articles.descriptionJa: ペイトリオッツは大敗を喫し、シーホークスは控えQBに敗北。パンサーズは怪我の影響を乗り越えられず、チャージャーズとテキサンズは0勝3敗に転落しました。昨シーズンのプレーオフ進出チームのうち5チームの今後はどうなるのでしょうか？
articles.body:
For the second time in three weeks, the opening window of the Sunday afternoon slate of NFL games delivered a delicious bowl of chaos. While Week 1 served up a record number of points, Week 3 brought upsets and heartbreaking defeats for teams that had lofty expectations heading into this season. Five teams that made the playoffs in 2025 lost games in crushing fashion.

Three of which -- the Chargers, Panthers and Texans -- held leads in the fourth quarter but couldn't hold them. A fourth -- the defending Super Bowl champ Seahawks -- lost to an 0-2 Commanders team that was down to its backup quarterback. And a fifth -- the defending AFC champ Patriots -- were blown out and appear to have secretly replaced their MVP candidate QB from a year ago with a startled, overwhelmed facsimile of Drake Maye. (The Rams also blew a 16-0 lead to the Broncos on Sunday night, but that was a narrow loss on the road to a team that also made last season's playoffs.)

Subscribe: 'The Bill Barnwell Show'

Today, I'm going to break down those five losses from teams that expected to be winning most of their games this season. Which defeat was most painful? Which raised the biggest questions about what happens next? I'll go from most crushing to least ominous, starting in Duval County, where the Jaguars (another 2025 playoff team) had no trouble stomping all over the Patriots.

Jump to:

Chargers | Panthers | Patriots

Seahawks | Texans

New England Patriots

Lost 35-6 to the Jaguars

On one hand, there's nothing unrealistic or shocking about the Patriots losing to the Jaguars in Jacksonville. On the other, unlike the other four games I'll talk about here, this loss wasn't particularly close. While Mike Vrabel & Co. might feel like they played better than the final score indicated and lost 10 points on sloppy play in the red zone and a missed field goal, the Patriots aren't building on what they put together in 2025. They look like they've gone back in time to the first half of the 2024 season, when Drake Maye was a rookie, Vrabel was out of football and a half-dozen dismal plays per game typically doomed them to losses.

Since A.J. Brown went down in the second half of the Week 1 loss to the Seahawks, the Patriots have looked like a completely different offense. Maye was playing well in that game, continuously taking checkdowns and small profits. With Seattle quarterback Drew Lock being summoned to play on short notice with Sam Darnold's early injury and the Seahawks struggling to score, that would have been a logical way for the Patriots to try to win.

Instead, Maye threw three interceptions to turn that game, all on throws he never should have considered making. He was better against the Steelers in Week 2 but badly underthrew a pass to Patrick Queen on a crosser for an interception, one play after he had escaped pressure and found Romeo Doubs on the sort of scramble drill creation Maye had excelled with last season.

articles.headline: NBA preview 2026-27: Stacking the 8 most intriguing newcomers
articles.description: A full roster's worth of NBA stars changed teams this past summer. The storylines surrounding eight will help define the league's journey to spring.
articles.headlineJa: 2026-27 NBAプレビュー：最も注目すべき新加入選手8選
articles.descriptionJa: この夏、ロースター1チーム分に相当するNBAスター選手たちが移籍しました。そのうち注目の8人を巡るストーリーが、春までのリーグの行方を決定づけるでしょう。
articles.body:
There will be plenty of familiar faces donning new jerseys on Monday when NBA media days unfold from coast to coast.

LeBron James and Giannis Antetokounmpo headline a group of six 2026 All-Stars who changed zip codes this summer. In all, 15 players with at least one All-Star selection in the past five seasons are set to take the court for new franchises. (This number includes Anthony Davis and Damian Lillard, who changed teams last season but have yet to play due to injuries.)

To make sense of all that furious player movement, let's run through the eight most intriguing newcomers for the 2026-27 season.

Note: These rankings consider each player's talent, his fit with his new team and other factors such as contract implications and championship expectations. Rookies have been excluded from this list.

1. Giannis Antetokounmpo, Miami Heat

Granted, Antetokounmpo's move to Miami didn't generate as much discussion as Luka Doncic's 2025 trade to the Los Angeles Lakers or LeBron James' latest decision to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers. Yet the two-time MVP deserves top billing from an intrigue standpoint; he was easily the best player to change teams this summer.

In fact, the "Greek Freak" was the only player in the top 12 of this year's NBA Rank who didn't return to the team he played for in 2025-26. And despite an injury-plagued final campaign in Milwaukee, the 31-year-old Antetokounmpo is still in his prime and was an All-NBA First-Team selection in 2024-25.

For those reasons, Antetokounmpo should face real championship expectations. He's about the same age as Shaquille O'Neal was when he joined the Heat in 2004, a move that paid off with a title two years later. Reaching the Finals at some point over the next four years seems like a reasonable benchmark for Antetokounmpo given that Jimmy Butler III led Miami to that stage in 2020 and 2023.

From a basketball standpoint, the Heat must continue building around a pair of star big men in Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo -- a strategic dilemma that's rare for contenders in the pace-and-space era.

Both players possess enough versatility to function together at a high level, but their partnership is bound to look different from any of Antetokounmpo's old Bucks teams or past editions of Adebayo's Heat. Miami could prove to be imposing, clunky or both.

Finally, Antetokounmpo's decision to virtually eliminate the 3-point shot from his scoring arsenal will make him a fascinating test case as he progresses through his 30s. The league's most successful elder statesmen in recent years include James, Kevin Durant, Stephen Curry, Kawhi Leonard, James Harden and Chris Paul, all of whom relied on the outside shot to extend their primes.

Is it possible to age gracefully and avoid recurring injuries while plowing through defenders on a nightly basis? Or will the Heat help Antetokounmpo discover useful adjustments that extend his prime and his team's championship window?

articles.headline: Sources: Giants' Brian Burns believed to have torn ACL
articles.description: New York Giants standout pass rusher Brian Burns is believed to have sustained a torn ACL during Sunday's 12-7 win over the Tennessee Titans, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
articles.headlineJa: 情報筋：ジャイアンツのブライアン・バーンズがACL断裂か
articles.descriptionJa: ニューヨーク・ジャイアンツの主力パスラッシャーであるブライアン・バーンズが、日曜日に行われたテネシー・タイタンズ戦（12-7で勝利）で前十字靭帯（ACL）を断裂したとみられると、複数の情報筋がESPNのアダム・シェフター記者とNFLネットワークのイアン・ラポポート記者に語りました。
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- New York Giants standout pass rusher Brian Burns is believed to have torn his ACL during Sunday's win over the Tennessee Titans, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

Burns went down with a knee injury in the fourth quarter of Sunday's 12-7 win. He crumbled to the ground when former teammate Austin Schlottmann went to block him in the chest. Burns immediately grabbed at his right leg and limped off with the help of teammates. He went straight into the locker room with the help of medical personnel.

Coach John Harbaugh told reporters after the victory that Burns would undergo an MRI to determine the severity of his injury. The Giants were crossing their fingers, much like they did for quarterback Jaxson Dart last week.

"There is some hope there, but we won't know until we see the MRI," Harbaugh said.

Burns, who came into the game with a low ankle sprain that kept him out of practice all week, is now likely out for the season. Kayvon Thibodeaux's role will increase greatly as a result of Burns' injury. Thibodeaux, the fifth overall pick in the 2022 NFL draft, started against the Titans with Burns limited to specific pass-rush packages.

Burns ranked second in the NFL in sacks (16.5) last season behind Myles Garrett. He is likely to finish this year with zero after recording at least 7.5 in each of his first seven NFL seasons. His loss will be a massive blow to a Giants defense that has just one sack this season.

The Pro Bowl edge rusher recorded four tackles through the Giants' first three games. He led the team with four pressures before exiting on Sunday, according to NextGen Stats.

"Everybody knows what Burns brings to the team," fellow edge rusher Abdul Carter said after Sunday's win. "I'm hoping it's nothing too bad."

The Giants were already dealing with a major injury on the offensive side after losing Dart for at least the regular season. Dart underwent surgery Friday to repair the meniscus and MCL in his left knee after being injured in Week 2.

Burns has not missed a game since the 2020 season and has totaled 71 sacks over his eight-year career. He played through numerous injuries last season and did the same on Sunday, intent on playing against the Titans even after not practicing all week and being listed as questionable with the ankle injury.

He came to the Giants in 2024 from the Carolina Panthers. He was traded for a second- and a fifth-round pick and was rewarded with a five-year, $150 million contract.

Quickly, he developed into one of the team leaders. Burns was a captain under former coach Brian Daboll and is on Harbaugh's leadership council (the Giants don't have captains) this year.

New York (2-1) will now have to attack the final 14 games of the season without perhaps its most important player on offense and defense.

"That really sucks," running back Cam Skattebo said Sunday. "It sucks to see anyone on the team go down, especially [Dart and Burns]."

articles.headline: Commanders set to re-add Austin Ekeler to RB room, sources say
articles.description: The Commanders are expected to sign free agent running back Austin Ekeler to their 53-man roster, pending a physical, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo.
articles.headlineJa: コマンダーズ、オースティン・エケラーをRB陣に再加入させる見込み 関係者が明かす
articles.descriptionJa: 関係者がNFLネットワークのイアン・ラポポート氏とマイク・ガラフォロ氏に語ったところによると、コマンダーズはメディカルチェックを経て、フリーエージェントのランニングバック（RB）オースティン・エケラーを53人のロースターに登録する契約を結ぶ見込みだという。
articles.body:
ASHBURN, Va. -- Austin Ekeler is set to return to Washington, as the Commanders are expected to sign the veteran running back, pending a physical, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo on Monday.

Ekeler played the past two seasons for Washington, but he ruptured his Achilles in Week 2 in 2025. He was a key offensive player for the Commanders in 2024 on their run to the NFC Championship Game but missed five games due to two concussions.

He worked out for the Carolina Panthers last week.

Ekeler was signed mostly for depth, and his role, as of now, remains uncertain. The Commanders have used Rachaad White as a third-down back. He injured his shoulder Sunday but did return and Ekeler's signing isn't related to that injury, according to a team source. White leads Washington with 151 yards from scrimmage, including 51 receiving.

Washington also has Jacory Croskey-Merritt, who has rushed for a team-high 142 yards this season, and rookie Kaytron Allen.

Injuries have impacted the past three seasons for Ekeler. He also missed three games in 2023 with the Los Angeles Chargers because of an ankle injury that affected him beyond the games he sat out.

But Ekeler was productive when healthy for the Commanders. In 14 games, he has caught 40 passes for 404 yards and rushed 91 times for 410 yards and four touchdowns. He averaged 31.3 yards on 19 kickoff returns in 2024, earning him second-team All-Pro honors.

Ekeler entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent signed by the Chargers in 2017. In seven seasons with the Chargers as an all-purpose back, he topped 1,000 yards from scrimmage in four seasons and surpassed 1,500 yards three times. In his nine-year career, Ekeler has gained 9,053 yards from scrimmage and scored 73 touchdowns.

articles.headline: Bulls trade Rob Dillingham to Hornets for Buddy Hield, cash
articles.description: The Bulls have traded Rob Dillingham to the Hornets for Buddy Hield and cash.
articles.headlineJa: ブルズ、バディ・ヒールドと金銭とのトレードでロブ・ディリンガムをホーネッツへ放出
articles.descriptionJa: ブルズは、バディ・ヒールドおよび金銭とのトレードでロブ・ディリンガムをホーネッツに放出した。
articles.body:
The Chicago Bulls have traded Rob Dillingham to the Charlotte Hornets for Buddy Hield and cash, the teams announced Sunday.

Dillingham, the No. 8 pick in the 2024 NBA draft and still just 21 years old, was moved less than a year after landing in Chicago at the trade deadline last season. He appeared in 30 games for the Bulls, averaging 9.6 points and 2.8 assists.

He could have a chance for a larger role in Charlotte, which traded longtime starting guard LaMelo Ball to the Minnesota Timberwolves earlier this offseason. Dillingham also joins the Hornets after Charlotte announced Friday that second-year guard Kon Knueppel has been sidelined with a hamstring injury.

The Hornets created a $9.6 million trade exception with the deal. 

Hield spent less than a week with the Hornets, who acquired the veteran sharpshooter from the Atlanta Hawks for Dorian Finney-Smith. Hield, known as a positive and high-energy player, has history with Bulls executive vice president Bryson Graham from their time together in New Orleans. 

Dillingham has one more year via a team option on his rookie contract before hitting restricted free agency in the summer of 2028. Hield has a player option worth around $10 million for the 2027-28 season.

articles.headline: Host Jalen Brunson gets assist from Knicks on 'SNL' premiere
articles.description: Jalen Brunson had four of his Knicks teammates -- Karl-Anthony Towns, Mikal Bridges, OG Anunoby and Josh Hart -- in the audience for his monologue Saturday night, in his role as host of "SNL."
articles.headlineJa: 『SNL』初回放送でホストを務めたジェイレン・ブランソン、ニックスのチームメイトからアシストを受ける
articles.descriptionJa: 土曜夜の『SNL』でホストを務めたジェイレン・ブランソンは、冒頭モノローグの際、観客席にニックスのチームメイト4人（カール＝アンソニー・タウンズ、ミカル・ブリッジズ、OG・アヌノビー、ジョシュ・ハート）を迎えた。
articles.body:
Jalen Brunson brought four of his NBA champion teammates to "Saturday Night Live."

The reigning NBA Finals MVP had four of his New York Knicks teammates -- Karl-Anthony Towns, Mikal Bridges, OG Anunoby and Josh Hart -- in the audience for his monologue Saturday night, in his role as host of the NBC program's 52nd season premiere.

Brunson poked fun at how he's not going to sing, how ESPN's Stephen A. Smith -- a Knicks fan, portrayed during the monologue by longtime "SNL" star Kenan Thompson -- owed him an apology for questioning his abilities and even quipped about how much he's looking forward to getting back to the Knicks' home court at Madison Square Garden.

"The exact spot where Taylor and Travis got married," Brunson said, referring to the summer wedding of Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce at the team's arena.

But the best assists came from Towns, Bridges, Anunoby and Hart, who all asked Brunson questions as part of the monologue.

Towns asked if someone could foul out of "SNL." When told it's not possible, Towns said, "So I can be here, like, the whole show? Nice."

Bridges asked Brunson if his arms were long, but lamented that he'll never fly. Anunoby, who got a huge ovation, asked Brunson if he recalled missing a shot late in Game 4 of the NBA Finals against San Antonio -- a series that the Knicks won in five games. The Game 4 shot that Anunoby was referring to was a last-second tip-in -- off a Brunson miss -- that basically ensured the Knicks would win the game.

"That was awesome," Anunoby said.

Hart, who co-hosts a podcast with Brunson, asked his New York teammate about how he left $113 million on the bargaining table when signing with the Knicks. Brunson, in turn, asked why Hart poked Brunson in the backside when the Knicks won the NBA Cup last season.

Brunson then brought his teammates to the stage for one last roar from the crowd.

Brunson became the first active NBA player to host the show since LeBron James -- then of the Cleveland Cavaliers -- in 2007, and the first pro athlete in the role since Kelce, the Kansas City Chiefs' tight end, in 2023.

The other NBA players to host besides Brunson and James: Michael Jordan in 1991, Charles Barkley on four occasions (including one as an active player in 1993) and Bill Russell in 1979. Russell's stint came 10 years after he retired as a player.

Brunson, Jordan, Barkley and James all hosted season premieres of "SNL." And Brunson promised to step up late, just like what he delivered in crunch time of the Knicks' games in the title series against the Spurs in June.

"I'm going to approach this the same way I approach a Knicks Finals game," Brunson said. "The first three quarters of the show are going to be god-awful. The last sketch is going to be amazing."

What's next for Curry and the Warriors?

Stephen Curry's two-year, $116 million extension made him the first player in NBA history to amass $600 million in career on-court earnings.

The deal has also put the Golden State Warriors in position to have extra spending power next summer.

By Curry taking $10 million less than the maximum allowed, the Warriors project to have nearly $38 million in cap space in 2027. Golden State could increase its projection to $55 million if center Kristaps Porzingis is waived in the offseason. Porzingis' $20 million salary for next season is guaranteed for $3 million.

For Golden State to have ample room, forwards Draymond Green and Jimmy Butler III would need to sign elsewhere or at a significantly lesser salary. They will be free agents next summer.

Both salary projections include the $17 million free agent hold of guard Brandin Podziemski. The 2023 first-round pick is eligible until Oct. 19 to extend his contract. -- Bobby Marks

If you're new to fantasy hoops and looking to try it out for the first time, here is a tutorial of all the basics. From there, it's easy to grab a handful of people, set up a draft and have some fun! Before that, though, it's always smart to spend a little time preparing with a mock draft of your own.

articles.headline: Which Premier League players got injured in the international break?
articles.description: All the latest news and updates on Premier League stars injuries during the first international break of the 2026-2027 club season
articles.headlineJa: 代表ウィーク中に負傷したプレミアリーグの選手は？
articles.descriptionJa: 2026-2027クラブシーズンの最初の代表ウィーク期間中に発生したプレミアリーグ主力選手の負傷に関する最新ニュースとアップデート。
articles.body:
Premier League teams will be watching and hoping their star players remain healthy throughout the international break.

However, some have already sustained injuries while playing for their countries. Premier League matches resume on Oct. 10.

ESPN will be tracking the latest injuries and updates for your club's players:

Kai Havertz (Arsenal)

Arsenal's Kai Havertz was forced off in the 30th minute of the game between Netherlands and Germany on September 24th with what was described as a muscle injury.

"Both are currently undergoing an MRI," Jurgen Klopp said on RTL about Havertz and Jamal Musiala. "I hope we get the diagnosis [on Thursday] evening. But of course, this isn't great. I hope it's nothing serious. The lads are probably out for us. But hopefully, they'll be back in action relatively quickly."

On September 25 the German Football Association confirmed the attacker would be leaving Klopp's camp and return to Arsenal after suffering what they describe as a 'muscle strain.'

Brian Brobbey (Sunderland)

The powerful Sunderland attacker was also injured in the same game after picking up what looked like a hamstring injury while running for the ball. He immediately went down and signalled to the sideline.

He left the field of his own accord but did have a heavy limp as he walked down the tunnel.

Netherlands boss Xavi Hernandez said after the game: "Brian is indeed injured."

Brobbey was replaced by Joshua Zirkzee in the Dutch squad.

Zion Suzuki (Aston Villa)

The goalkeeper linked up with the Japan squad but according to reports missed the main group training session on September 22nd, according to local reports. Instead he was put on an individual session for a rib injury.

Suzuki was subsequently left out of Japan's matchday squad entirely for Thursday's 3-1 victory over Uruguay.

Dan Ballard (Sunderland)

The Sunderland defender suffered a reported hamstring injury during Northern Ireland's 1-0 victory over Georgia in the UEFA Nations League.

With the score still 0-0 as the match moved into stoppage time, Ballard chased back as Georgia counter-attacked and pulled up clutching the back of his thigh, unable to finish the match in Tbilisi.

Speaking immediately after Friday's match, manager Michael O'Neill said it was too soon to know the extent of his latest injury but will definitely miss the next three Northern Ireland games.

"We'll scan him tomorrow (Saturday), but he's certainly not going to be available for the next three games."

Alexander Isak (Liverpool)

Alexander Isak is returning to Liverpool after sustaining a "minor injury" on international duty.

The striker scored and played the full 90 minutes in Sweden's 2-1 victory over Romania in the Nations League on Friday.

But Isak, who has made a strong start to the season for Liverpool, will not feature in matches against Poland, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Romania over the remainder of the extended international break.
